title: A finite filtration with injective graded pieces admits a compatible splitting
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $a\le b$ be integers, and let $(I,F)$ have a decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration] with $F^aI=I$ and $F^{b+1}I=0$. Suppose that $\operatorname{gr}^n I=F^nI/F^{n+1}I$ is injective in the extension-property sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions] for every $a\le n\le b$. There exist injective objects $J_n$ for $a\le n\le b$, isomorphisms $J_n\cong\operatorname{gr}^n I$, and an isomorphism $\theta:I\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{n=a}^b J_n$ identifying $F^pI$ with the sub-biproduct $\bigoplus_{a\le n\le b,\ n\ge p}J_n$ for every integer $p$.

source.place: Tag 05TP, lemma-filtered-injective; the specified interval and identification of J_n with gr^n I follow from its displayed split filtration

proof.text: Put $J_n=\operatorname{gr}^n I$ for $n\in[a,b]$, and let $q_n:F^nI\to J_n$ be the cokernel of $F^{n+1}I\to F^nI$. Since $J_n$ is injective, extend $q_n$ along the monomorphism $F^nI\to I$ to a map $f_n:I\to J_n$. For $p>n$, the composite $F^pI\to I\xrightarrow{f_n}J_n$ vanishes: factor through $F^{n+1}I\to F^nI$ and use the cokernel relation. This is exactly the extension property in the definition of injectivity (Mathlib Injective.factorThru and comp_factorThru), without any injectivity assertion about the filtration steps.

source.place: Tag 05TP, lemma-filtered-injective; omitted finite-filtration splitting argument expanded by extending graded coordinate maps and descending induction

proof.text: For every integer $p$ put $B_p=\bigoplus_{n\in[a,b],\ p\le n}J_n$ and define $\alpha_p:F^pI\to B_p$ by the coordinates $F^pI\to I\xrightarrow{f_n}J_n$. The vanishing in Step 1 shows that $\alpha_p$ commutes with the next-step filtration inclusion and the tail inclusion $d_p:B_{p+1}\to B_p$. Explicitly, compare each projection: at $n\ge p+1$ the two coordinates are the same inclusion followed by $f_n$; at $n=p$ they both vanish. For $a\le p\le b$, projection onto the $p$-coordinate gives a split short exact sequence $0\to B_{p+1}\xrightarrow{d_p}B_p\to J_p\to0$. Its retraction is restriction to coordinates $n\ge p+1$, its section is the $p$-summand inclusion, and their two complementary idempotents sum to the identity, as checked on each biproduct coordinate.

source.place: Tag 05TP, lemma-filtered-injective; omitted finite-filtration splitting argument expanded by extending graded coordinate maps and descending induction

proof.text: Prove that $\alpha_p$ is invertible for $a\le p\le b+1$ by descending induction. For $p=b+1$, its source is zero by the upper filtration bound and its target is an empty biproduct, hence it is invertible. At a successor step compare the short exact sequence $0\to F^{p+1}I\to F^pI\xrightarrow{q_p}J_p\to0$ with the split short exact sequence of Step 2. The left vertical map is $\alpha_{p+1}$, invertible by induction; the middle map is $\alpha_p$; the right vertical map is the identity of $J_p$. The left square commutes by Step 2, and the right square commutes because the $p$-coordinate restricts to $q_p$ on $F^pI$. Apply the short five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-short-five-lemma] to get invertibility of $\alpha_p$.

source.place: Tag 05TP, lemma-filtered-injective; omitted finite-filtration splitting argument expanded by extending graded coordinate maps and descending induction

proof.text: Let $\beta:I\to B=\bigoplus_{n\in[a,b]}J_n$ have coordinates $f_n$, and let $j_p:B_p\to B$ be the canonical tail inclusion. Comparing coordinates and using Step 1 gives $(F^pI\to I)\beta=\alpha_pj_p$ for every integer $p$. At $p=a$, the filtration inclusion is invertible by $F^aI=I$, $\alpha_a$ is invertible by Step 3, and $j_a$ is invertible because every index lies in the tail. Hence $\beta$ is invertible. Take $\theta$ to be this isomorphism, the already chosen injective $J_n$, and their identity graded-piece isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 05TP, lemma-filtered-injective; omitted finite-filtration splitting argument expanded by extending graded coordinate maps and descending induction

proof.text: For $a\le p\le b+1$, the factorization in Step 4 and invertibility of $\alpha_p$ give $\operatorname{im}((F^pI\to I)\theta)=\operatorname{im}(j_p)$; this is the required equality of subobjects, not merely of abstract objects. If $p<a$, decreasingness and $F^aI=I$ give $F^pI=I$, and $j_p$ is an isomorphism because all indices are in the tail, so both subobjects are top. If $p>b+1$, the tail is empty, so $j_p=0$; the factorization in Step 4 makes both images zero. This covers every integer $p$, including the empty tail at the upper endpoint.

lean.statement: theorem injective_graded_filtration_splits {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (X : FilteredObject C) (a b : ℤ) (hab : a ≤ b) (ha : X.filtration.F a = ⊤) (hb : X.filtration.F (b + 1) = ⊥) (hgr : ∀ n : Set.Icc a b, Injective (X.filtration.gradedPiece n.1)) : ∃ J : Set.Icc a b → C, (∀ n : Set.Icc a b, Injective (J n)) ∧ (∀ n : Set.Icc a b, Nonempty (J n ≅ X.filtration.gradedPiece n.1)) ∧ ∃ θ : X.obj ≅ @biproduct _ C _ _ J (HasBiproduct.of_hasProduct J), ∀ p : ℤ, (Subobject.map θ.hom).obj (X.filtration.F p) = imageSubobject (@biproduct.fromSubtype _ C _ _ J (HasBiproduct.of_hasProduct J) (fun n : Set.Icc a b ↦ p ≤ n.1) (HasBiproduct.of_hasProduct _))
